NIO’s Deliveries Fell 15% in October, Ending a 31-Month Growth Streak. Here’s the One Brand Behind the Entire Drop
sum: - Analyst Ratings: 11 Buy, 5 Outperform, 6 Hold, 1 Underperform

NIO (NIO) delivered 34,246 vehicles in October, down 15.2% from a year earlier. It was the company’s first year-over-year decline since February 2024, ending 31 straight months of growth. Rivals set records the same month: Xpeng (XPEV) passed 50,000 for the first time with 50,237, and Leapmotor (9863) delivered 106,127. All of NIO’s year-over-year drop came from ONVO, its family brand. The premium NIO brand and Firefly both grew.
NIO released the figures on Sunday, November 1, after shares closed at $3.21 on October 30. The stock is down 37.06% in 2026 and sits 13.2% below the lowest Wall Street target TIKR tracks.

October 2025 was a hard comparison. It was NIO’s first month above 40,000 deliveries, lifted by a then-record 17,342 ONVO cars. This October, the NIO brand delivered 18,125 (up 5.7%), and the compact Firefly brand delivered 7,738 (up 30.9%). ONVO fell 51.7% to 8,383. That 8,959-car drop is larger than the company’s entire 6,151-car decline.

The NIO brand is not off the hook. It fell 15.0% from September’s 21,318, more than the company’s total month-over-month decline. ONVO has slipped every month since July’s 10,155. It supplied 24.5% of October’s cars, against CEO William Li’s long-term goal of 55% of group sales, according to Electric-vehicles.com.

On the September 1 earnings call, Morgan Stanley analyst Tim Hsiao asked how NIO would lift ONVO’s orders. Li, speaking through an interpreter, said ONVO would remain a premium family brand. He said NIO would not be very aggressive in entering the entry-level segment and would balance sales volume against vehicle gross margin. He also said a major new ONVO model is due in 2027.

October alone doesn’t show whether ONVO’s slide reflects that pricing discipline or weaker demand. Li Auto’s deliveries also fell, by 8.6% to 29,025, but Xpeng grew 19.6% and Leapmotor 51.0%, so the market explains only part of it.

Nio Stock Slides In Hong Kong As EV Maker Admits Flaws In Europe Expansion Plan Amid Sales Slump
sum: Shares of Nio, Inc. (NIO) fell over 2% in Hong Kong on Wednesday after a senior executive admitted to errors in the company’s European expansion plans, even as the EV maker accelerates product launches in China.
U.S.-listed shares of Nio rose 0.2% to $5.30 on Tuesday but pared those gains, slipping 0.4% in extended trading.

Mark Zhou, Nio’s executive vice president, said on the ‘Leaders Unplugged’ podcast, hosted by David Bach, President of IMD Business School, that the company incorrectly assumed that early success in Norway could be replicated across the wider European Union.

“We started with Norway because Norway is one of the best locations for the electric vehicle industry,” Zhou said. “With that kind of success, we thought Norway was the same as the European Union, which turned out to be totally different.”

Zhou said Nio underestimated differences in consumers, governments and regulations, and acknowledged that some of its vehicles were poorly suited to European cities. “A lot of our vehicles are big because they’re more tailored to the Chinese environment,” he said, adding that European teams warned the cars were difficult to maneuver in narrow urban areas.

Norway has highlighted the challenges, with Nio missing its 2025 delivery target by about 65%. Across Europe, registrations remain minimal, including just 56 vehicles in January and a single registration in Germany, despite multiple flagship showrooms.

Zhou also said infrastructure costs and slower regulatory processes hurt the rollout. “We didn’t anticipate the speed and we didn’t anticipate the total cost of setting it up,” he said, citing Europe’s stricter rules, including GDPR compliance. Firefly, Nio’s compact sub-brand developed in Munich, has seen limited European traction and has since been redirected to China, where it now sells about 6,000 units per month.

Nio's Sales Are Rising but 18.5% Is the Key Number to Watch When Q3 Earnings Arrive
sum: For Nio (NIO -0.62%) investors, selling more vehicles is encouraging, especially as it needs scale to break even for the full year 2026, as management has targeted. But turning those sales into sustainable profits? That's where the automotive industry gets challenging.

The electric vehicle (EV) maker delivered 109,178 vehicles during the third quarter, increasing 25.4% year over year, according to its delivery update. That's solid growth, but investors already know the delivery total. The upcoming earnings report needs to tell us more about the financial quality of those sales.
One figure deserves particular attention: vehicle margin. Nio has made substantial progress on that front, and protecting those gains could matter more than investors realize.

Bear with me for a little investing 101. Vehicle margin simply measures the percentage of vehicle revenue remaining after the associated cost of sales. It tells investors how much of that revenue remains to cover expenses such as research, development, and marketing. Nio's vehicle margin reached 18.5% in the second quarter, up from 10.3% a year earlier and 18.8% in the first quarter of 2026. The longer trend shows how far the business has come, and it's impressive, even with some bumps along the way.

There are reasons to believe Nio can defend its vehicle margin gains, in part thanks to rising premium-brand deliveries. During its second-quarter earnings call, management said its premium ES8 and ES9 SUVs each generated vehicle margins above 20%.

Further, third-quarter deliveries of the namesake Nio brand increased approximately 69% year over year, outpacing Firefly's roughly 52% growth, while Onvo deliveries declined approximately 26%. That shifted the premium brand's share of deliveries from about 42% to 57%. If that shift favors higher-margin models such as the ES8 and ES9, it should help support the company's recent vehicle margins above 18%.

But there is a bit of a catch. Management also highlighted rising costs for memory chips, batteries, and other materials. Its stated aim during the earnings call was to keep third- and fourth-quarter vehicle margins around the second-quarter level.

- The bank said some buyers likely waited for the five-seat ES8, while the phaseout of a 10,000 yuan purchase-tax subsidy also hurt demand.

U.S.-listed shares of Nio, Inc. (NIO) are looking to snap a four-week losing streak after Deutsche Bank said that softer ES8 deliveries drove June’s shortfall, while the EV maker’s second-quarter breakeven target remains within reach.
Nio’s U.S.-listed stock snapped three sessions of gains on Wednesday to end 2% lower at $4.97.

Deutsche Bank attributed the miss mainly to the ES8 SUV, estimating June deliveries at about 8,900 units. The bank said that some buyers likely waited for the five-seat ES8, which entered showrooms and opened preorders on June 28, while the phaseout of Nio’s 10,000 yuan purchase-tax subsidy also weighed on demand, according to CnEVPost.
The weakness was partly offset by newer models. The main Nio brand delivered 21,908 vehicles in June, up 9% month-on-month, while Onvo delivered 11,743 units and Firefly rose 23% to 6,946 units.
